description: Mobile development knowledge for React Native, Expo, Flutter, native Android/iOS, mobile UI, app performance, and release workflows.

sections.name: React Native and Expo
sections.explanation_simple: React Native builds mobile apps using React components backed by native iOS and Android views. Expo adds a managed toolchain for faster setup, previewing, builds, notifications, camera, sensors, and app store packaging.
key_concepts: React Native: React components rendered as native mobile views
Expo: managed React Native toolchain and cloud build service
Metro bundler: JavaScript bundler used by React Native
Native module: bridge to platform-specific APIs
EAS Build: Expo app build pipeline for Android and iOS
Navigation: stack, tab, drawer, and deep-link routing

code_examples.title: Expo App Startup
code_examples.code:
npx create-expo-app my-mobile-app
cd my-mobile-app
npx expo start

sections.learning_path: React basics -> Expo app -> navigation -> device APIs -> EAS build -> store release

sections.name: Mobile UI and Performance
sections.explanation_simple: Mobile UI must be fast, touch-friendly, and stable across screen sizes. Performance depends on reducing rerenders, using virtualized lists, compressing images, avoiding heavy work on the main thread, and testing on real devices.
key_concepts: Touch target: interactive area large enough for fingers
Safe area: screen region outside notches and system bars
Virtualized list: renders only visible rows for large lists
Offline state: usable behavior when network drops
Device testing: verification on real Android and iOS hardware

code_examples.title: FlatList for Large Lists

sections.learning_path: Responsive layout -> safe areas -> list performance -> image optimization -> offline handling -> release QA

sections.name: Native Android and iOS Release Flow
sections.explanation_simple: Production mobile release requires signing keys, bundle identifiers, permissions, privacy declarations, crash reporting, store screenshots, staged rollout, and rollback planning.
key_concepts: Android package name: unique app identifier
iOS bundle ID: unique Apple app identifier
Permissions: declared access to camera, location, contacts, or storage
Staged rollout: releases to a small percentage before full launch
sections.learning_path: App identifiers -> signing -> permissions -> store assets -> beta test -> staged rollout

topics.name: React Native capability note
topics.content: Tom can currently provide React Native and Expo implementation guidance. Full execution requires external Node/Expo CLI availability and platform build credentials.
